learning_outcomes.description: Evaluate production practices used in commercial nursery crop production.
Explain the factors that shape the horticultural industry with reference to associated cultural and management practices.
Evaluate the positive and negative interactions of invertebrates with horticulture crops pre- and post-harvest.
Describe postharvest factors affecting fruit and vegetable quality, shelf life, and produce losses/wastage.
Prepare a solution proposal addressing a contemporary challenge relating to production horticulture.
Communicate scientific solutions clearly in both written and spoken forms to a general audience.

assessments.task_description:
Students are to prepare a proposal and justification for the introduction of a new horticultural plant species for cultivation under Australian climatic conditions. As a horticulture consultant working for a company in Australia you are tasked to explore a possible new horticultural plant that could be suggested to growers, as an alternative to existing commodity plants (such as avocado, citrus, table grapes, mango, etc.), for those that would like to diversify their production base. This plant should be resilient and be adapted to unpredictable climates, particularly dominated by increased temperature and water scarcity. The produce should have the potential to be marketable to consumers that demand sustainably produced, high-quality products, and have strong export potential.

Guide for preparing the report

Introduction

Identify, introduce and justify the importance and benefits associated with the production of the proposed plant. You will need to search the literature, and ideally include statistics and scientific information from the literature to provide a reasoned and clear argument for growing the new plant you have selected. You should also highlight any gaps in the current knowledge. In the final paragraph, restate why the plant should be introduced, including how the new plant will benefit the horticultural industry.

Body

Describe the environmental and other production requirements, whilst also considering ecological adaptations that make this plant a suitable choice. Based on the growing requirements of the plant, consider the regions where the plant could be grown in Australia. Identify possible markets and other financial, social and environmental benefits associated with this new plant. Also, highlight any challenges that you foresee with the introduction of the plant, and possible solutions to overcome such hurdles.

Conclusion

Summarise the main points covered in your report and restate the relevance of your proposed plant to the horticultural industry, society and the environment.

Reference list

The majority of your papers should be published within the last 10 years. You are welcome to use any referencing style, provided you are consistent, or you may use the style set by the American Psychological Association style (APA). The most recent version of APA is the APA 7th style. https://guides.library.uq.edu.au/referencing/apa7

General Presentation

Your report should be prepared with headings and subheadings to provide structure and clarity. The case study should be typed using 12-point Times New Roman / Calibri /Arial and 1.5 line spacing.

Length: 2500 words +/- 10%, not including figures, tables, and reference list. Please, see assessment guidelines and marking criteria in the Blackboard course site for specific instructions.

assessments.task_description:
Students are required to prepare a 3 minute PowerPoint presentation based on your 'New horticultural plant development plan' assignment. In this assessment task, you will give a mock presentation to your company CEO or Board of Directors stating the plant you have identified, the benefits of introducing the new plant for the company and consumers (e.g. new markets), the changes (e.g. labour, equipment, technology) that would need to be made to introduce the new plant, limitations and potential solutions. Conclude by restating the benefits of the new plant to the company, the horticulture industry, environment and society.

The presentation will be given during the scheduled class lecture/practical in person (face-to-face).

Skills in giving oral presentations are important because during your career as you are likely to present at work meetings, industry gatherings and conferences. You will find that everytime you present, it will become easier, and presenting on a regular basis helps ease any nervousness you might have.

Guide for preparing the presentation

For a 3-minute presentation (plus 2 mins for questions), aim to have no more than 5 slides, excluding a title slide and a reference slide. Your slides should include the following:

Introduction

Provide a concise overview of the topic and outline the main sections you will be covering in your presentation.

Body

For your new plant, you should include new scientific findings - such as current technologies, new developments and recent research. Research data should be presented clearly using graphs and/or tables. You should critically review the data you present and compare the results to other studies, where possible. Include in-text references to acknowledge sources where necessary.

Conclusion

Summarise the main points of your presentation and restate the benefits for the new plant.

Reference list

Include a list of references, on a separate slide, at the end of your presentation. You are welcome to use any referencing style, provided you are consistent, or you may use the style set by the American Psychological Association style (APA). The most recent version of APA is the 7th edition.  https://guides.library.uq.edu.au/referencing/apa7 

General advice

Your presentation should be reportable in a 5-minute time slot. Within this period, you should talk for 3 minutes and answer questions for 2 minutes.

PowerPoint presentations should be visually attractive and use images to explain your points rather than typed words. Keep word use to a minimum and use a clear font, such as Arial or Courier. Avoid reading directly from slides as it prevents you from connecting with your audience.

Practice your presentation beforehand. Use language that is listener-friendly and scenarios that people can easily relate to. Pretend that you are describing your work to your parents or your best friend who is not necessarily a horticulturist but is educated and interested. Add a little humor to keep the presentation entertaining and interesting. Use voice tone and hand gestures to transmit information. Please, see assessment guidelines and marking criteria in the Blackboard course site for specific instructions.

The use of AI or MT must be referenced appropriately. Please see assessment guidelines in blackboard course site for specific instructions. Students may also refer to Library guides found under Additional assessment information > Acknowledging and referencing AI use.
